# components/reveal

Import: `import { Reveal, RevealGroup, Parallax, LazySection, ScrollProgress, CountUp, ScrollSteps } from "@tundralibs/ui/reveal"`

Shown on its demo page (`deno task build:demos`, then `demo/components/reveal.html`). Guides: [Getting started](../UI-Getting-Started.md) · [rAPId integration](../UI-Rapid.md) · [Theming](../UI-Theming.md).

## Functions

### `Reveal`

```ts
Reveal(props: RevealProps): Html
```

Content that arrives as it scrolls into view. Moved only under
`html.js` (a page without the script shows everything at once), and
never transparent unless `hide` (or a `fade` / `blur` effect) says so;
reveal.js adds `is-revealed` when the block enters the viewport, so the
effect never costs a plain page anything. Blocks already on screen at
load reveal immediately.

### `RevealGroup`

```ts
RevealGroup(props: RevealGroupProps): Html
```

A row or list of blocks that reveal one after another.

### `Parallax`

```ts
Parallax(props: ParallaxProps): Html
```

A block that drifts against the scroll — a hero image, a decorative
panel. reveal.js moves it with a transform while it is on screen,
throttled to animation frames. It stays still under reduced motion and
on coarse pointers (phones): a transform per scroll frame on a phone
fights the browser's own scroll compositing and judders. Overflow is
the caller's to clip: give the parent `overflow: hidden` or let the
block bleed.

### `LazySection`

```ts
LazySection(props: LazySectionProps): Html
```

A section that loads when it is about to be seen, not on page load — a
long landing page's lower bands. With the rAPId runtime on the page
reveal.js calls `window.rapid.swap(action, section)` as it nears the
viewport (unlike `data-load`, which fetches on mount). On a plain page
there is no runtime: the section keeps its placeholder, so give it
content worth keeping (static sections need no loading at all) —
reveal.js marks it `data-lazy-inert` and moves on.

### `ScrollProgress`

```ts
ScrollProgress(props = …: ScrollProgressProps): Html
```

A thin reading-progress bar fixed to the viewport's edge, filling as
the page (or `target`) scrolls past. Pure CSS where
`animation-timeline: scroll()` exists and no target is set; reveal.js
otherwise writes `--scroll-progress` on each scroll frame. Decorative:
`aria-hidden`, and a screen reader never hears it.

### `CountUp`

```ts
CountUp(props: CountUpProps): Html
```

A figure that counts up to its value as it scrolls into view — a stat on
a landing page. The markup carries the final, formatted number (a plain
page, a crawler and a reduced-motion user all read the figure itself);
reveal.js animates from `from` once on first sight, writing the same
`Intl.NumberFormat` output each frame, and ends on the exact text it
was given. `format: "percent"` takes a fraction (0.42 → 42%).

### `ScrollSteps`

```ts
ScrollSteps(props: ScrollStepsProps): Html
```

Scrollytelling: a column of steps beside a sticky stage whose media
cross-fades as each step scrolls through the middle of the viewport.
The first step is current in the markup; reveal.js makes the step whose
text is nearest the viewport's middle current (`aria-current="step"`,
`is-active`), so the stage and the text on screen always agree. A
heading that opens a step is drawn at `--scroll-steps-title-size`.
Below 768 the stage is hidden and each step shows its own media in
flow — the story reads top to bottom with nothing sticky. Only the
current media on the stage is visible, so only its controls take focus;
focus inside a picture moves to the new picture as the step changes.

## Types

### `RevealEffect`

How a revealed block arrives: fade in place, rise from below, grow from 96%, or sharpen from a blur.

- `"fade"`
- `"rise"`
- `"scale"`
- `"blur"`

### `RevealDelay`

A delay before the reveal plays, in steps of 80 ms (classes, never an inline style).

- `"0"`
- `"1"`
- `"2"`
- `"3"`

### `RevealTag`

The element the reveal renders as.

- `"div"`
- `"section"`
- `"li"`
- `"span"`

### `RevealProps`

| Prop | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `content` | `Html` | yes |  |
| `effect` | `RevealEffect` |  |  |
| `delay` | `RevealDelay` |  |  |
| `once` | `boolean` |  | Reveal once and stay (default). `false` hides it again when it scrolls out, so it replays on the way back. |
| `tag` | `RevealTag` |  |  |
| `hide` | `boolean` |  | Start the block transparent until it is in view. Off by default, so text wrapped in a reveal is always readable — a fast scroll can pass a heading before it arrives; `rise` and `scale` only move it. Turn it on for media and decoration. (`fade` and `blur` always hide: that is all they do.) @default false |
| `attrs` | `Attrs` |  |  |

### `RevealGroupProps`

| Prop | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `items` | `Html[]` | yes | Each item becomes its own `Reveal`. |
| `effect` | `RevealEffect` |  |  |
| `stagger` | `boolean` |  | Stagger the items: reveal.js numbers each child (`--reveal-index`, through the CSSOM) and the stylesheet delays it by that many steps. |
| `once` | `boolean` |  |  |
| `hide` | `boolean` |  | Each item starts transparent (see `RevealProps.hide`). @default false |
| `tag` | `"div" | "ul"` |  | The group element. @default "div" |
| `attrs` | `Attrs` |  |  |

### `ParallaxSpeed`

How far a parallax block drifts against the scroll: a tenth, a fifth or a third of the distance.

- `"slow"`
- `"medium"`
- `"fast"`

### `ParallaxProps`

| Prop | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `content` | `Html` | yes |  |
| `speed` | `ParallaxSpeed` |  |  |
| `attrs` | `Attrs` |  |  |

### `LazySectionProps`

| Prop | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | `string` | yes | Required: the swapped region keeps this id. |
| `action` | `string` | yes | The fragment URL rAPId fetches once the section nears the viewport. |
| `placeholder` | `Html` | yes | What shows until then — a Skeleton, or static content a plain page keeps. |
| `rootMargin` | `string` |  | How far ahead of the viewport to fetch. @default "200px 0px" |
| `attrs` | `Attrs` |  |  |

### `ScrollProgressPosition`

Which edge of the viewport the reading-progress bar sits on.

- `"top"`
- `"bottom"`

### `ScrollProgressProps`

| Prop | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | `string` |  |  |
| `position` | `ScrollProgressPosition` |  |  |
| `target` | `string` |  | A selector for the element whose reading the bar tracks — an article. Without it the bar tracks the whole page, and a browser with scroll-driven animations draws it with no script at all. |
| `attrs` | `Attrs` |  |  |

### `CountUpDuration`

How long a counted number takes to arrive: 600 / 1200 / 2000 ms.

- `"fast"`
- `"base"`
- `"slow"`

### `CountUpFormat`

How a counted number is written: with a locale's grouping, compacted (1.2K), as a percent, or as money.

- `"number"`
- `"compact"`
- `"percent"`
- `currency:${string}`

### `CountUpTag`

The element a counted number renders as.

- `"span"`
- `"strong"`
- `"b"`

### `CountUpProps`

| Prop | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `value` | `number` | yes | The figure the number arrives at — rendered in full in the markup. |
| `from` | `number` |  | Where the count starts. @default 0 |
| `duration` | `CountUpDuration` |  |  |
| `format` | `CountUpFormat` |  |  |
| `locale` | `string` |  | `Intl` locale for grouping and currency; the page's `lang` when unset. |
| `decimals` | `number` |  | Decimal places; inferred from the value when unset. |
| `tag` | `CountUpTag` |  |  |
| `attrs` | `Attrs` |  |  |

### `ScrollStepsHeight`

How tall each step's scroll band is: 60 / 80 / 100 vh.

- `"sm"`
- `"md"`
- `"lg"`

### `ScrollStep`

| Prop | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `content` | `Html` | yes | The step's text — a heading and a paragraph. |
| `media` | `Html` |  | What the sticky stage shows while this step is current. It renders twice, in the step and on the stage, with only one displayed at any width: ids (and what refers to them) get a prefix on the stage copy. Fields would post twice, so a form does not belong here. |

### `ScrollStepsProps`

| Prop | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | `string` | yes | Required: the step ids derive from it. |
| `steps` | `ScrollStep[]` | yes |  |
| `height` | `ScrollStepsHeight` |  |  |
| `stage` | `"start" | "end"` |  | Which side the stage sits on at ≥ 768. @default "end" |
| `label` | `string` |  | Accessible name of the step list. @default "Steps" |
| `dim` | `boolean` |  | Mute the text of the steps that are not current. `false` keeps every step at full text colour — only the stage's picture changes. @default true |
| `attrs` | `Attrs` |  |  |

## Usage

Each example as the rAPId call and the HTML it renders — the markup a plain page writes by hand. Icons are inline SVG in the real output; they are shortened to `<svg …>…</svg>` here.

### A section that rises into view

A rise only moves the block: the heading is readable from the first frame, even when a fast scroll passes it before it arrives. A page without the script shows it in place.

```ts
Reveal({
  content: html`
    <h2>Why teams switch</h2>
  `,
  effect: "rise",
  tag: "section",
})
```

```html
<section class="reveal" data-reveal="rise">
  <h2>Why teams switch</h2>
</section>
```

### A picture that fades in

`hide: true` starts the block transparent — for media and decoration, never for the text a reader is scanning.

```ts
Reveal({
  content: html`
    <img src="/img/map.png" width="960" height="540" alt="Clicks by country" loading="lazy">
  `,
  hide: true,
})
```

```html
<div class="reveal" data-reveal="rise" data-reveal-hide="">
  <img src="/img/map.png" width="960" height="540" alt="Clicks by country" loading="lazy">
</div>
```

### Three cards, one after another

```ts
RevealGroup({
  items: ["Send", "Chase", "Collect"].map((t) =>
    Card({
      title: t,
      body: html`
        <p>…</p>
      `,
    })
  ),
  stagger: true,
})
```

```html
<div class="reveal-group" data-reveal-group="" data-reveal-stagger="">
  <div class="reveal" data-reveal="rise">
    <div class="card">
      <div class="card__content">
        <div class="card__header">
          <div class="card__heading">
            <div class="card__title">Send</div>
          </div>
        </div>
        <div class="card__body">
          <p>…</p>
        </div>
      </div>
    </div>
  </div>
  <div class="reveal" data-reveal="rise">
    <div class="card">
      <div class="card__content">
        <div class="card__header">
          <div class="card__heading">
            <div class="card__title">Chase</div>
          </div>
        </div>
        <div class="card__body">
          <p>…</p>
        </div>
      </div>
    </div>
  </div>
  <div class="reveal" data-reveal="rise">
    <div class="card">
      <div class="card__content">
        <div class="card__header">
          <div class="card__heading">
            <div class="card__title">Collect</div>
          </div>
        </div>
        <div class="card__body">
          <p>…</p>
        </div>
      </div>
    </div>
  </div>
</div>
```

### A band that loads as it nears the viewport

With the rAPId runtime the section swaps in `/fragments/customers`; a plain page keeps the placeholder.

```ts
html`
  ${Parallax({
    content: html`
      <img src="/img/texture.png" width="1200" height="400" alt="">
    `,
    speed: "slow",
  })}${LazySection({ id: "customers", action: "/fragments/customers", placeholder: SkeletonCard() })}
`
```

```html
<div class="parallax" data-parallax="0.1">
  <img src="/img/texture.png" width="1200" height="400" alt="">
</div>
<section class="lazy-section" id="customers" data-lazy-section="" data-action="/fragments/customers">
  <div class="skeleton-card" aria-busy="true">
    <span class="skeleton skeleton--block" aria-hidden="true"></span>
    <span class="skeleton skeleton--title" aria-hidden="true"></span>
    <span class="skeleton skeleton--text skeleton--w-full" aria-hidden="true"></span>
    <span class="skeleton skeleton--text skeleton--w-half" aria-hidden="true"></span>
  </div>
</section>
```

### Stats that count up

The markup carries the final figure; reveal.js counts from 0 once the number is seen.

```ts
html`
  <p>${CountUp({ value: 12840, tag: "strong" })} invoices sent · ${CountUp({
    value: 0.98,
    format: "percent",
    duration: "slow",
  })} paid on time</p>
`
```

```html
<p>
  <strong class="count-up" data-count-up="12840" data-count-duration="1200" data-count-decimals="0">12,840</strong>
  invoices sent ·
  <span class="count-up" data-count-up="0.98" data-count-duration="2000" data-count-format="percent" data-count-decimals="2">98.00%</span>
  paid on time
</p>
```

### A reading-progress bar and a scrollytelling section

`ScrollProgress` without a target is CSS-only where scroll timelines exist; `ScrollSteps` stacks below 768.

```ts
html`
  ${ScrollProgress()}${ScrollSteps({
    id: "how-it-works",
    height: "md",
    steps: [
      {
        content: html`
          <h3>Send</h3>
        `,
        media: html`
          <img src="/img/send.png" width="800" height="600" alt="">
        `,
      },
      {
        content: html`
          <h3>Collect</h3>
        `,
        media: html`
          <img src="/img/collect.png" width="800" height="600" alt="">
        `,
      },
    ],
  })}
`
```

```html
<div class="scroll-progress" data-scroll-progress="" aria-hidden="true">
  <div class="scroll-progress__bar"></div>
</div>
<section class="scroll-steps scroll-steps--md" id="how-it-works" data-scroll-steps="">
  <ol class="scroll-steps__list" aria-label="Steps">
    <li class="scroll-steps__step is-active" id="how-it-works-step-1" data-scroll-step="0" aria-current="step">
      <div class="scroll-steps__text">
        <h3>Send</h3>
      </div>
      <div class="scroll-steps__inline-media">
        <img src="/img/send.png" width="800" height="600" alt="">
      </div>
    </li>
    <li class="scroll-steps__step" id="how-it-works-step-2" data-scroll-step="1">
      <div class="scroll-steps__text">
        <h3>Collect</h3>
      </div>
      <div class="scroll-steps__inline-media">
        <img src="/img/collect.png" width="800" height="600" alt="">
      </div>
    </li>
  </ol>
  <div class="scroll-steps__stage">
    <div class="scroll-steps__media is-active" data-scroll-step-media="0">
      <img src="/img/send.png" width="800" height="600" alt="">
    </div>
    <div class="scroll-steps__media" data-scroll-step-media="1">
      <img src="/img/collect.png" width="800" height="600" alt="">
    </div>
  </div>
</section>
```

## Behaviour

`components/reveal/reveal.js` ships in `ui.js` (delegated on `document`, re-initialised after a rAPId swap).

Attributes it reads or writes: `data-action`, `data-count-decimals`, `data-count-duration`, `data-count-format`, `data-count-from`, `data-count-locale`, `data-count-up`, `data-counting`, `data-lazy-inert`, `data-lazy-loading`, `data-lazy-margin`, `data-lazy-section`, `data-parallax`, `data-reveal`, `data-reveal-repeat`, `data-reveal-stagger`, `data-scroll-progress`, `data-scroll-step`, `data-scroll-step-media`, `data-scroll-steps`.

Events: `rapid:swapped`.
